question: Which of the following therapeutic options is currently considered the most effective for the treatment of a chronic infection of a hip arthroplasty and achieve a functional recovery?

options.opa: Intravenous antibiotics for three weeks, followed by oral antibiotics for six more weeks.
options.opb: Removal of the infected prosthesis, surgical debridement, placement of a spacer, antibiotherapy and after a while placement of a new prosthesis.
options.opc: Surgical debridement followed by antibiotherapy for 12 weeks without removing the prosthesis.
